chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari from Al-Husayn ibn al-Mundhir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'My wife gave me money to manage, so I should buy a slave girl from her wealth whom I may have sexual relations with.' He said, then he said: 'She intended to cool your eye (give you pleasure) and warm her own eye (secure her status/pleasure).'

key_terms.أَطَأُهَا: I have sexual relations with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a husband using his wife's personal wealth to buy a slave girl for himself?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the marital dynamic where a wife provides capital for her husband to acquire a slave girl, interpreting the act as a gesture of mutual affection and security. This reflects the pre-modern socio-economic context where such acquisitions were common for household management and concubinage, emphasizing the wife's agency in enhancing marital harmony through financial contribution. The Imam’s concise response highlights the underlying emotional and social benefits ('cooling' and 'warming' the eye) rather than merely the legal transaction.
